Reason: The chest X-ray demonstrates bilateral, patchy areas of airspace consolidation that are predominantly located in the peripheral and lower lung zones. This peripheral and basilar distribution is a classic radiographic hallmark of cryptogenic organizing pneumonia (COP), making option D the most accurate description and correlation.
